Article Title: AI can never perform core job of judgment writing: SC judge
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court's most senior judge, Justice Vikram Nath, on Sunday said artificial intelligence could at best be a facilitator for the justice delivery system but could never replace the core task - writing judgments - which would always remain with judges.Speaking on 'Challenges, innovations and role of AI in judicial governance' at the Supreme Court Bar Association's first national conference in Bengaluru, Justice Nath said, "AI can be used as a tool to augment the judicial system, but it cannot replace the judgment or judges' minds as to what is to be decided."Justice Nath said, "There can be no fixed data set in millions of cases dealt by courts. Take, for example, matrimonial cases, settlement of commercial cases, balancing equities - the court can understand the nuances of each case, which is factually different from the other, by reading papers and hearing the counsel.Judges alone know how to strike a balance in family partition suits."He added, "AI cannot decide cases involving constitutional issues. There are innumerable complexities in criminal cases - how to appreciate the evidence, when to grant bail; in the same FIR there can be 10 accused, court may grant bail to nine but deny one. AI can't deal with all these. AI is there to help us in several aspects - collate data, categorise cases, translations etc.But the judgment will remain with judges only. "Justice Nath also commended the initiative taken by SCBA president Vikas Singh on the conference.SC judge A G Masih said, "AI is not here to replace lawyers and judges. Data-driven intelligence cannot replace human conscience. The act of the courts rests on public faith to deliver justice by carefully balancing rights and liabilities and undertaking an assessment of factual circumstances with a human heart. Feelings cannot be replicated by AI, which can facilitate judicial activities but cannot substitute them. "The judge said there seemed to be a need to institutionalise guidelines for court technology and, perhaps, create a judicial-tech oversight board to maintain and check AI tools for bias and to review an automated draft.Senior advocate Sajan Poovayya said hallucination was implicit in mankind and mankind made AI. Therefore, hallucination was also implicit in AI and it was that which made it dangerous for the judiciary as it presented case law and logic that was non-existent or imaginary, he said.Delhi HC Chief Justice D K Upadhyay brought up the use of AI-assisted judgment drafting software in countries like Brazil, Argentina, Singapore, the UK, the UAE and China. "Collectively, AI is increasingly integrated in multiple domains of judicial governance from administrative efficiency to substantive support functions, while simultaneously raising important questions about accountability, fairness and limits of automation in the judicial system," he said.Justice Upadhyay added, "AI-manipulated images, deepfakes deployed maliciously undermine the integrity of evidence and adversely impact administration of justice. Courts may have to re-examine the traditional reliance on photographs and videos... Burden on parties to establish authenticity will increase and the judiciary would have to rely more on forensic tests of such evidence."
Article Summary: Supreme Court's most senior judge, Justice Vikram Nath, on Sunday said artificial intelligence could at best be a facilitator for the justice delivery system. Justice Nath said there seemed to be a need to institutionalise guidelines for court technology and, perhaps, create a judicial-tech oversight board.

Article Title: Aravind Srinivas: Perplexity AI CEO Aravind Srinivas, who once made $30 billion-plus offer to buy Google Chrome browser, now says: Google search does a much better job than anyone else in the world
Article Text:
Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas revealed his company's Comet browser on iOS defaults to Google Search for navigational queries, acknowledging Google's superior performance in these areas. This pragmatic approach positions Comet as a complementary tool, blending Google's speed with Perplexity's advanced AI capabilities for more complex needs.

Comet on iPhone keeps Google search , layers Perplexity on top

A $34.5 billion bid that went nowhere—and a browser that launched anyway

Last August, Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas wrote a letter to Sundar Pichai offering $34.5 billion for Google 's Chrome browser—a figure that was nearly double Perplexity's own valuation at the time. Seven months later, on the same day his company launched the iPhone version of its Comet browser, Srinivas posted something that cuts right against the narrative of an all-out war with Google: on Comet iOS, Google is the default search engine. And he's not apologetic about it."Google does a much better job here than anyone else in the world, including Perplexity," Srinivas wrote on X, specifically calling out navigational searches—think finding a restaurant nearby, checking a sports score, or hunting for a hotel deal.These are the everyday, quick-hit queries that make up the bulk of mobile browsing, and Srinivas is openly conceding that Google has them wrapped up.The Comet iOS app—now free, after the desktop version debuted last summer at $200 a month—takes a different approach from the PC version, which does not default to Google. Srinivas explained the thinking: the browser blends Google's "navigational speed and breadth of verticals" with Perplexity's answer quality and multimodal capabilities.The Comet Assistant sits on top of any webpage, including Google's own results page, ready to jump in when a navigational answer isn't what you need. Voice mode access is baked in too.Technically, Comet is still built on Chromium—the same open-source engine that powers Chrome, Edge, and a stack of other browsers—but Srinivas says the UI and interactions are all native, putting it closer to Safari-level polish on iOS. Native ad blocking and background video playback round out the feature set.The Chrome acquisition saga ended quietly in September 2025 when US District Judge Amit Mehta ruled that Google does not need to divest either Chrome or Android. Perplexity, meanwhile, kept building. The Comet browser is now available across iPhone, Android, Windows, and Mac, with no native iPad app yet.What makes Srinivas's latest comments interesting isn't the praise for Google—it's the pragmatism. Rather than positioning Comet as a Google killer, he's framing it as the browser that knows when to hand off to Google and when to step in itself. That's a harder pitch to make, but probably an honest one.
Article Summary: Comet on iPhone keeps Google search, layers Perplexity on top. CEO Aravind Srinivas: "Google does a much better job here than anyone else in the world" Comet is now available across iPhone, Android, Windows, and Mac, with no native iPad app yet.

Article Title: WeChat meets OpenClaw: Tencent launches tool to bring AI agent to app
Article Text:
What is OpenClaw and why it matters



AI agents in China



Why the AI agent race matters



Tencent has launched a tool that will bring an AI agent directly into WeChat – China’s most popular messaging app that has over one billion monthly active users even as the company pushes into one of the hottest battlegrounds in Chinese technology right now. The tool, called ClawBot, integrates Tencent's WeChat platform with OpenClaw, an open-source AI agent capable of performing tasks on a user’s behalf, according to a report by news agency Reuters. ClawBot appears as a contact within WeChat, which means users can open a chat and start sending commands to the AI agent.OpenClaw is an open-source AI agent that has gained traction in recent weeks as users across China rush to install and experiment with agent-based AI products.The surge in interest has prompted China’s major tech companies to quickly explore business opportunities in the space even as Chinese authorities have flagged concerns about the security risks that come with AI agents.A report claimed that the rush to try OpenClaw has also increased the demand for second-hand Macbooks. AI agents can take actions like performing tasks, automating processes and operating on behalf of users across digital systems.Earlier in March, the company unveiled its own AI agent suite comprising three products: QClaw for individual consumers, Lighthouse for developers and WorkBuddy for enterprise customers. The WeChat-OpenClaw integration now adds another dimension of having an external agent directly into the social platform.China’s biggest tech companies are all moving aggressively into AI agents, and the pace of launches over the past week alone illustrates how fierce the competition has become. Alibaba last week launched Wukong, an AI platform for enterprises that coordinates multiple AI agents simultaneously to handle complex business tasks within a single interface.Baidu quickly followed with a series of AI agents built on OpenClaw, spanning desktop software, cloud services, mobile tools, and smart-home devices.AI agents represent a meaningful evolution beyond the chatbot era. Where chatbots respond to questions, agents take initiative – meaning that users can give a goal and they work toward it autonomously, completing multi-step tasks across different applications and services.
Article Summary: Tencent has launched a tool that will bring an AI agent directly into WeChat. The tool, called ClawBot, integrates Tencent's WeChat platform with OpenClaw, an open-source AI agent. China's biggest tech companies are all moving aggressively into AI agents.

Article Title: Meta shuts down Horizon Worlds: Almost 5 years after CEO Mark Zuckerberg called it 'the next frontier' for the company, Meta is shutting down Horizon Worlds; says: We are separating ...
Article Text:
A costly Metaverse bet of the company

Meta’s steps to streamline Quest experience

Meta Horizon Worlds: By March 31, 2026, Horizon Worlds and Events will no longer appear in the Store on Quest. Also, Horizon Central, Events Arena, Kaiju, and Bobber Bay worlds will no longer be available in VR. You can still jump into your other favorite worlds in VR until June 15, 2026, after which the Horizon Worlds app will be removed from Quest, and Worlds will no longer be available in VR. After June 15, you can jump into all your favorite mobile-optimized worlds on the Meta Horizon mobile app.

Your existing captures will remain viewable within the Hyperscape Capture (Beta) app and the companion Preview app, which are available in your Quest app library. You can continue capturing new Hyperscapes, but sharing, inviting, and co-experiencing Hyperscapes with others will no longer be supported.

Meta Horizon Plus (MH+) Perks: By March 31, 2026, Horizon-specific perks — including Meta Credits, Digital Clothing, Avatars and In-World Purchases — will be removed from the subscription. Your core MH+ gaming benefits and monthly games will not be affected,” said Meta.

Watch Mark Zuckerberg SCOLDED During Senate Hearing Over ‘Vile’ Social Media Content; ‘You've Blood...' Mark Zuckerberg SCOLDED During Senate Hearing Over ‘Vile’ Social Media Content; ‘You've Blood...'

Nearly five years after Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg hailed Horizon Worlds as “the next frontier” for the Facebook-parent, the company has announced that it is now shutting down the virtual reality social network for Quest headsets. In a community blog post, Meta noted that the Horizon Worlds app will be removed from the Quest store at the end of March and fully discontinued on VR devices by June 15, 2026. After that date, the platform will continue only as a standalone mobile app, which Meta says will allow each platform to “grow with greater focus.” “Earlier this year, we shared an update on our renewed focus for VR and Horizon. We are separating the two platforms so each can grow with greater focus, and the Horizon Worlds platform will become a mobile-only experience.This separation will extend across our ecosystem, including our mobile app. To support this vision, we are making the following changes to streamline your Quest experience throughout 2026,” said Meta in a blog post.Facebook-parent Meta launched the Horizon Worlds in late 2021 as a central piece of Meta’s pivot to the metaverse. The app offered a 3D social space where avatars could easily interact and play games. Despite the heavy investment, the platform struggled to attract users and it never really managed to surpass a a few hundred thousand monthly actives.Horizon World was managed by Meta’s Reality Labs unit which posted billions in quarterly losses since its reception. In January, the division reported an operating loss of $6.02 billion. Weeks later, Meta cut more than 1,000 employees from Reality Labs, including staff at Ouro Interactive, an in-house studio that had been building first-party content for Horizon Worlds.In September 2023, Meta also started offering a mobile version of Horizon Worlds. With this move, the company aimed to model the platform after platforms like Roblox to reach users without VR headsets. The company now says it will focus almost exclusively on mobile, while continuing to support VR developers separately. Samantha Ryan, Vice President of Content at Reality Labs, explained in a February blog post: “By breaking things down into two distinct platforms, we’ll be better able to clearly focus on each. ”In the blog post, Meta also streamlined the process of maintaining the Quest experience. “To support this vision, we are making the following changes to streamline your Quest experience throughout 2026.
Article Summary: Facebook-parent Meta launched Horizon Worlds in late 2021 as a central piece of Meta’s pivot to the metaverse. The app offered a 3D social space where avatars could easily interact and play games. Despite the heavy investment, the platform struggled to attract users and never really managed to surpass a a few hundred thousand monthly actives.

Article Title: Andrew Bosworth : Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth on Meta changing its plan of shutting down Horizon Worlds: Community was adamant that ...
Article Text:
Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth

Meta announcement of shutting down VR Horizon Worlds access in June



Meta had a change of heart just less than 48 hours after the company publicly confirmed to fans that it was pulling the plug on Horizon Worlds for VR. Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth said that Horizon Worlds for Quest will stick around for the "foreseeable future".On backtracking on the earlier announcement to shut down the VR version of Metaverse, Andrew “Boz” Bosworth explained on an Instagram AMA the community was adamant that they wanted to have access to Horizon Worlds on Meta Quest headsets. “We have decided, just today in fact, we will keep Horizon Worlds working in VR for existing games,” Bosworth said. He added that the Horizon Unity runtime games that currently exist will continue to operate in VR and won’t be ported to mobile platforms.At the same time, Meta isn’t currently planning on making any more Horizon World games for VR. And that’s because “the creator and consumer energy were already big on mobile,” he said.Bosworth also wrote an Instagram post on the same. In his post, Bosworth said, "We will keep Horizon Worlds working in VR for existing games, to support the fans who've reached out." He added, "For people who already have games they like that they're using in Horizon Worlds, [they] will be able to download the Horizon Worlds app and use it in VR for the foreseeable future."Bosworth also said that there was "a lot of misinformation" about the company's plans. "We announced, 'hey, we're moving away from Horizon Worlds in VR,' and the headline is that Horizon is dead," he said. "It's not. And likewise, VR is not dead. We're continuing to invest tremendously."He described Metaverse as a "misunderstood concept" that was never meant to only encompass virtual reality. "When somebody is using their phone and you're physically with them, they're at the dinner table with you, and yet when you talk to them, they hear nothing because they've transported themselves through the glowing rectangle into a digital space," he said. "Maybe that they're scrolling media, maybe that they're in the text world, but like they have transported themselves. So we've always had this internally — at least me and Mark — this very expansive construct of the Metaverse," added Bosworth.Earlier Meta announced that Horizon Worlds will be inaccessible via virtual reality headset after June 15, 2026. The company shared plans to separate Horizon Worlds from Quest VR platform and focus exclusively on the smartphone version of the app in February and last week in a new post on its community forums, Meta detailed when the VR version of Horizon Worlds will be deprecated. It said that by March 31, individual Horizon Worlds and Events will no longer be listed in the Quest's Store and headset owners will be unable to visit worlds like "Horizon Central, Events Arena, Kaiju and Bobber Bay. " Then, after June 15, the app will be removed from Quest headsets and worlds will be completely unavailable to visit in VR. From that point on, the easiest place to visit Horizon Worlds will be in the Meta Horizon app for iOS and Android.
Article Summary: Earlier Meta announced that Horizon Worlds will be inaccessible via virtual reality headset after June 15, 2026. The company shared plans to separate Horizon Worlds from Quest VR platform and focus exclusively on the smartphone version of the app in February. On an Instagram AMA, Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth said the company will keep Horizon Worlds working in VR for existing games, to support the fans who've reached out.

Article Title: US cyber security agency gives deadline to Federal agencies to fix Darksword spyware threat on Apple devices
Article Text:
Critical flaws linked to active attacks

CVE-2025-31277 Apple Multiple Products Buffer Overflow Vulnerability

CVE-2025-32432 Craft CMS Code Injection Vulnerability

CVE-2025-43510 Apple Multiple Products Improper Locking Vulnerability

CVE-2025-43520 Apple Multiple Products Classic Buffer Overflow Vulnerability

CVE-2025-54068 Laravel Livewire Code Injection Vulnerability

What is DarkSword

US cyber security agency Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added five new security flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) list, warning that these are being actively used by hackers. The vulnerabilities that include Darksword spyware impacted Apple products and web platforms such as Craft CMS and Laravel Livewire. Authorities have warned that these weaknesses might enable hackers to seize control of systems or compromise sensitive information. Federal agencies are mandated by government regulations to address these problems by April 3, 2026. This action underscores the escalating threats posed by sophisticated cyberattacks aimed at commonly used software and hardware.Among the newly added issues is a major flaw in Craft CMS (CVE-2025-32432) with a top severity score. It allows attackers to run harmful code remotely.Another flaw in Laravel Livewire (CVE-2025-54068) allows attackers to execute commands without needing login access.CISA also flagged multiple Apple-related issues affecting iOS, macOS and Safari. These can be triggered using harmful web content, often used in targeted attacks.The five new vulnerabilities include:Darksword is reportedly a professionally designed, highly sophisticated platform that appears to have been built for future development and shows clear signs of deliberate engineering for maintainability. Security researchers call Darksword an exploit kit that has tools designed to take advantage of vulnerabilities in software, in this case Apple’s iOS.The group behind Darksword is tracked by researchers under the identifier UNC6353 and a definitive attribution remains unclear. Researchers say that there are signs that large language model (LLM) tools – which power AI chatbots – have been used to extend Darksword's functionality.
Article Summary: US cyber security agency has added five new security flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) list. Authorities have warned that these weaknesses might enable hackers to seize control of systems or compromise sensitive information. Federal agencies are mandated by government regulations to address these problems by April 3, 2026.

Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu shares why giving employees more freedom can feel ‘chaotic’; says ‘There is always …’
Article Text:
Sridhar Vembu on why freedom can feel ‘chaotic’

Sridhar Vembu: 'Every smart programmer’ thinks they can do better

Here’s the post shared by Sridhar Vembu

Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has shared his views on a workplace question many companies face: Should employees wait for instructions from their leaders or take the initiative and act on their own? In a post on X (formerly known as Twitter), Sridhar Vembu said giving people more freedom to take initiative can create an energetic but sometimes chaotic work culture. Employees may disagree strongly with one another and constantly feel that things can be improved. “There is always the gnawing feeling of ‘not good enough’,” Vembu wrote, explaining the trade-off between certainty and initiative in an organisation.In the post, Sridhar Vembu said highly metric-driven organisations often create a culture where employees wait for instructions from the top. Such workplaces can offer more predictability and certainty.However, he warned that this approach has its risks. “Unless the top always knows how to set the right course, the org can be lost,” Vembu wrote.On the other hand, an organisation where people are encouraged to take initiative can be less predictable. Employees with energy and strong ideas may disagree with each other, he said.“Seize the initiative culture” often feels chaotic, with lots of internal disagreements.There is always the gnawing feeling of “not good enough”,” Vembu wrote.The Zoho founder also used programmers as an example to explain why initiative-driven workplaces can see frequent disagreements.“People who are full of energy and initiative often vehemently disagree with other,” he wrote, adding: “I joke about this: every smart programmer looks at another programmer's code and thinks ‘it sucks, I can do better’!”According to Vembu, this is the trade-off companies need to understand when building their culture. A workplace can provide employees with comfortable certainty but risk losing their initiative. Alternatively, it can encourage people to take initiative while accepting the discomfort and disagreements that may come with it."On org culture: Do people wait for instructions from the top? Or do they seize the initiative and run?Highly metric driven orgs tend to produce the "wait for instructions from the top" culture and there is more predictability and certainty in that culture. Unless the top always knows how to set the right course, the org can be lost."Seize the initiative culture" often feels chaotic, with lots of internal disagreements. There is always the gnawing feeling of "not good enough". In a chaotic initiative-driven culture, the external environment (market) may have to provide the occasional discipline.People who are full of energy and initiative often vehemently disagree with other. I joke about this: every smart programmer looks at another programmer's code and thinks "it sucks, I can do better"!That is your trade-off in org cultures. We can provide comfortable certainty but lose the initiative or we can seize the initiative but keep feeling somewhat uncomfortable.In my experience, trying to square this circle: "we will have a highly disciplined culture of seizing the initiative" produces the worst of both worlds."
Article Summary: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu says giving people more freedom to take initiative can create an energetic but sometimes chaotic work culture. “There is always the gnawing feeling of ‘not good enough’,” he wrote, explaining the trade-off between certainty and initiative in an organisation.

Article Title: Looking to improve your TV's picture quality? These 5 setting changes can help
Article Text:
AI generated image for representation

Start with the right picture mode

Turn off motion smoothing for movies

Carefully adjust brightness and contrast

Don't increase sharpness too much

Check energy-saving and automatic brightness

Many people spend hours watching movies, shows and sports on their TV, but only a few make the most of their screen’s picture quality. The good news is that users do not need expensive equipment or professional calibration to improve their TV picture. A few simple changes to picture mode, brightness, motion settings and sharpness can make movies, shows and sports look more natural and detailed. Here are some of the most important TV settings to change for better picture quality.The first setting to check is Picture Mode. Most TVs offer options such as Standard, Vivid, Dynamic, Sports, Movie, Cinema and Filmmaker Mode. These modes generally aim for a more accurate and natural-looking image. Filmmaker Mode, where available, also reduces extra picture processing. Vivid and Dynamic modes may look eye-catching, but they can push brightness and colours too far for regular viewing.If movies look unusually smooth, almost like a soap opera or live television, motion smoothing could be the reason. This feature adds extra frames to make movement appear smoother.Motion processing can be useful in some situations, but many viewers prefer to switch it off or lower it when watching films.It might be called MotionFlow or Picture Clarity, depending on the brand of your TV.The brightness and contrast can make a big difference to what you see on screen. Contrast affects highlights and bright areas, while brightness or black level setting affects how much detail is visible in dark scenes.A good approach is to use a familiar movie or show with both dark and bright scenes.More sharpness does not always mean more detail in the picture quality. Instead, it can add artificial outlines around objects and make the image look unnatural. Hence, it is recommended to lower the sharpness setting. Having said that the best level can vary by TV and personal preference.Some TVs automatically adjust screen brightness depending on the room lighting or energy-saving settings. While these features can help in reducing power consumption, they may also make the picture look dim.If the screen appears inconsistent, checking features such as ambient light sensors, adaptive brightness or energy-saving modes may help. Available settings and names differ between TV brands and models.
Article Summary: The first setting to check is Picture Mode. Most TVs offer options such as Standard, Vivid, Dynamic, Sports, Movie, Cinema and Filmmaker Mode. Vivid and Dynamic modes may look eye-catching, but they can push brightness and colours too far for regular viewing. Some TVs automatically adjust screen brightness depending on the room lighting or energy-saving settings.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness.

Article Title: From silver keepsakes to personalised bands, here’s what’s trending this Raksha Bandhan
Article Text:
This year’s rakhi designs reflect a blend of tradition and modernity, showcasing upgraded styles with luxurious materials. The trend of silver and bracelet-like rakhis marks them as lasting tokens for brothers. Eco-friendly handcrafted varieties add a rustic charm, while personalized options featuring initials and photos elevate the sentiment. Classic symbols such as the Evil Eye and Ganesha remain favored among wearers, merging spirituality with personal expression.

SILVER TAKES CENTRE STAGE:

RAKHIS THAT LOOK LIKE BRACELETS:

BACK TO HANDMADE:

MAKE IT PERSONAL:

THE PROTECTIVE CHARM:





This Raksha Bandhan, the humble rakhi is getting a stylish makeover. While the festival remains rooted in the sibling bond, designs are evolving with changing tastes; from jewellery-inspired and personalised bands to eco-friendly, handcrafted options.The rakhi is no longer just a ceremonial thread but a keepsake and style statement. Whether it’s a silver one, a minimalist bracelet or a handmade band, this year’s designs blend tradition with contemporary style.Premium rakhis crafted in 925 sterling silver are emerging as keepsakes rather than one-day accessories. Paired with American Diamond (AD) embellishments, intricate motifs and polished finishes, these rakhis can double up as a piece of jewellery long after the festival. “This year I bought a silver rakhi for my brother. It has a tiny Ganesha pendant-like thing with red threads attached. I loved the fact that this beautiful rakhi will be something that can stay with him even after the festival,” says Dimple Mojis, an entrepreneur from Goregaon. The appeal lies in their combination of sentiment, durability and a premium aesthetic.One of the biggest shifts is towards rakhis designed to be worn beyond Raksha Bandhan.“I am glad that I got to pick a bracelet rakhi. There’s a variety available this year right from sleek chain-link bands, adjustable metal cuffs and watch-style straps that give the traditional thread a contemporary, jewellery-like appeal. My brother is a GenZ and he likes understated menswear accessories. These designs offer a way to retain the rakhi as an everyday piece rather than putting it away after the festival,” says Preety Shah, working professional from Bangur Nagar.At the other end of the spectrum, handcrafted and eco-friendly rakhis are finding their place. Crochet and handwoven designs, rudraksha beads, wooden elements and biodegradable seeds bring a rustic, earthy character to the festival. "I have four cousin brothers for whom I picked up handmade rakhis. I like looking beyond mass-produced accessories, and these offer that handmade, artisanal feel,” says Antara Gupta, an entrepreneur-artist, from Vikhroli.Personalisation is another defining trend this year. Initials, names, photographs and customised messages are being incorporated into rakhi bands, turning them into more intimate mementoes. An engraved initial or a photograph can make a relatively simple design feel unique, particularly for siblings who want the rakhi to carry a personal story. “I found many options of ordering personalised rakhis for my brother this year, online. Article Title: Fraudster uses Raigad SP’s WhatsApp display photo to dupe police staff, seeks Rs 50,000
Article Text:
A cyber fraudster impersonated Raigad SP on WhatsApp, targeting police personnel for money transfers, but the scam attempt was foiled. (AI-generated image)





NAVI MUMBAI: Raigad Cyber Police have registered a case against an unidentified fraudster who allegedly used the WhatsApp Display Picture (DP) of Raigad Superintendent of Police (SP) Anchal Dalal to deceive several police personnel into transferring money.On Thursday, the fraudster sent a message to Raigad SP's reader, PSI Siddheshwar Murkute, asking him to transfer money urgently. Murkute immediately realised that it was a modus operandi commonly used by cyber scammers, as the WhatsApp message was sent from an international number that was not saved in his mobile phone.Thereafter, PSI Murkute learnt that the same scammer had sent similar messages to several Raigad police personnel. Fortunately, no one fell prey to the fraud, as the police personnel were aware of this modus operandi used by cyber fraudsters.Subsequently, PSI Murkute registered an FIR against the unidentified accused under the relevant section of the BNS for the offence of cheating by personation.The complainant, PSI Murkute, said, "I had received the WhatsApp message from an international number and the DP was of Raigad SP Anchal Dalal.The message read, 'I am in a meeting and my mobile is switched off. Immediately transfer Rs 50,000 to my bank account.' I knew the message sender was a scammer. I deliberately replied asking for the bank account number by pretending to send the money. As I received the bank account number from the scammer, it will be useful for the cyber police team to trace the bank account holder. "PSI Murkute added, "One police officer had received a WhatsApp message from the same international number asking to transfer Rs 2,000 by impersonating SP madam and claiming that it was required for filling diesel in the car, and that her mobile battery had drained and she was unable to pay online at the fuel station."API Amol Jadhav of Raigad Cyber Police said, "The cyber scammers use VPNs (Virtual Private Networks) to mask their identity. However, the Internet Protocol (IP) address of the WhatsApp number used by the accused will be obtained to trace the location, and the accused will soon be behind bars."
Article Summary: A cyber fraudster impersonated Raigad SP on WhatsApp, targeting police personnel for money transfers. Fortunately, no one fell prey to the fraud, as the police personnel were aware of this modus operandi used by cyber fraudsters. One police officer received a WhatsApp message from the same international number asking to transfer Rs 2,000 by impersonating SP madam.

Article Title: Cantonment water supply staffer duped of Rs38,000
Article Text:
Pune:





Two bike-borne men in helmets posed as police constables to dupe a Cantonment water supply department staffer out of Rs38,000 around 3.40am on Sunday. The suspects pretended to check the complainant’s phone to con him.The complainant, a contractual staffer with the department registered an FIR with the Wanowrie police on Monday evening.Wanowrie police senior inspector Pandit Rejitwad said, “The complainant works at the Cantonment water pumping station and reaches his workplace around dawn. After starting the pumping units, he and two of his colleagues went for a walk when the suspects approached them and conned him.”“They asked the complainant, a native of Uttar Pradesh , and his friends some basic questions and questioned their presence in the area. Article Title: ANPR camera system launched in Namakkal district to curb traffic violations
Article Text: NAMAKKAL: An automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) camera system was launched in Namakkal district on Monday to impose fines on traffic violators. The facility was inaugurated at the Namakkal–Salem Road corner junction by district superintendent of police Yadav Krish Ashok.The ANPR system will automatically detect violations such as using mobile phones while driving, riding w-wheelers without helmets and driving without seat belts. Fines will be issued digitally. The penalty amount and receipt will be sent directly to the violator’s registered mobile number.Speaking to reporters, S P Yadav Krish Ashok said, “Road accidents have claimed 348 lives in Namakkal district in the past eight months. Strict monitoring is essential to reduce fatalities. The ANPR camera system will help enforce discipline among motorists. Riders must wear helmets for their own safety and that of their families. Those indulging in reckless stunts will also be closely monitored and penalised.”
Article Summary: The facility was inaugurated at the Namakkal–Salem Road corner junction by district superintendent of police Yadav Krish Ashok. The ANPR system will automatically detect violations such as using mobile phones while driving, riding w-wheelers without helmets and driving without seat belts.

Bell Labs was working on car-based phones, while Cooper and Motorola were developing a device a person could carry. By making the call in the middle of a street rather than from a vehicle, Cooper demonstrated the idea of a truly portable mobile phone.In the 1970s, Bell Laboratories was developing mobile phones designed for use inside cars. Motorola was pursuing a different approach that would allow people to carry their phones with them.Cooper's 1973 call was made using an early prototype that would eventually lead to the Motorola DynaTAC 8000X. The first mobile phone sold to consumers did not arrive until 1984, more than a decade after Cooper made his call.The DynaTAC 8000X was considerably different from the phones people use today. It could provide around 30 minutes of talk time, required about 10 hours to recharge and weighed roughly 1.7 pounds. Its price was also high, equivalent to about $11,700 in today's money.The 1973 demonstration was therefore not a consumer product launch. It showed that a mobile phone could operate independently of a vehicle and be carried by an individual.Cooper later explained that the call had a broader purpose beyond the competition between Motorola and Bell Labs. Article Title: One key opens hundreds of cabins stocked with food across Norway, where no roads, staff or reception exist, only trust
Article Text:
​Representative Image of serene Norwegian mountain cabins surrounded by vast wilderness (AI-generated image)

How 1 standard key came to open hundreds of different Norwegian cabins

Why self-service and no-service cabins stock completely different supplies

How an offline payment system and a chore list keep the trust system working

Why Norway's cabin trust system rests on far more than 1 honest hiker

Deep in the Norwegian mountains, a hiker can reach a locked wooden cabin with no road leading to it, no receptionist and often no phone signal at all. A single small metal key still opens the door. That same standard key works across hundreds of cabins run by Den Norske Turistforening, the Norwegian Trekking Association known as DNT. Once the lock turns, what follows looks less like checking into a hotel and more like temporarily taking over a shared household. Inside a self-service cabin, shelves may hold oatmeal, crispbread, pasta, canned soup, coffee and snacks, all left unattended and meant to be paid for honestly. The visitor records what they take, pays once they regain phone signal, fetches water, tends the stove, cleans up before leaving and stacks fresh firewood for whoever arrives next, a stranger they will likely never meet, trusting that the same system will be waiting for them on their next journey through Norway's remote wilderness. This remarkable system exemplifies how mutual trust and collective responsibility can sustain vast networks of shared resources, offering a compelling model for community-driven cooperation elsewhere.According to DNT's own explanation of the cabin key system, the standard key unlocks hundreds of the organisation's unstaffed and self-service cabins across Norway. Members can obtain one for a small deposit and keep it while their membership remains active. The key provides access to participating cabins, although not every DNT property uses the same system. Some cabins remain unlocked, while others use a special key, code lock or booking-specific instructions. Cabins can also close temporarily or seasonally because of hunting, landowner agreements or wildlife protection, including measures intended to avoid disturbing migrating wild reindeer. DNT therefore advises hikers to check the individual cabin's listing before setting out.According to DNT's guide to its cabin types, the network broadly includes staffed lodges, self-service cabins and no-service cabins, a distinction that matters more than it might first appear. Self-service cabins provide sleeping and cooking facilities alongside a stocked food pantry, with products priced individually and guests expected to record everything they take. No-service cabins generally provide bunks, blankets, cooking facilities and firewood, but no food for sale, meaning hikers need to bring their own provisions. Staffed lodges are different again, with hosts and served meals available during their operating season, so the same DNT network can take a hiker from a fully stocked pantry at one stop to an entirely self-sufficient kitchen at the next.DNT's cabin-payment system is designed around the fact that mobile coverage can disappear precisely where many of these cabins are located. According to DNT's guide to its cabin app, visitors can record their cabin stay and purchases while offline and complete payment once their phone reconnects to a network. The system therefore depends heavily on visitors honestly recording what they have used, with no cashier or attendant standing beside the pantry shelves.The same principle applies to maintaining the cabins. According to DNT's cabin-visit guide, guests are expected to handle many of the ordinary chores themselves, including fetching water, tending the wood stove, washing dishes and cleaning the spaces they use. Before leaving, visitors are asked to leave the cabin ready for the next person, including cleaning used areas and preparing firewood. The expectation is simple: the next hiker should find the cabin at least as good as the previous visitor found it.The scale behind the system is considerable. According to DNT's own history, the organisation was founded in 1868 to make Norwegian nature easier and more affordable to experience. Today, its network includes more than 600 cabins spread across mountain ranges, forests, coastlines and former farmsteads throughout the country.The system works because the responsibility is distributed. Local member associations, volunteers and cabin wardens help restock food, repair buildings, maintain paths, split firewood and keep the properties functioning. Every hiker who records their purchases, cleans a room, carries water or prepares wood is therefore contributing to a much larger system that depends on thousands of small acts of cooperation. The remarkable part is not really that one key can open hundreds of doors. It is that behind each door is an unwritten agreement: take what you need, pay what you owe, clean up after yourself and leave something useful for the stranger who comes next.
Article Summary: Den Norske Turistforening, the Norwegian Trekking Association known as DNT, runs hundreds of self-service cabins across the country. The organisation was founded in 1868 to make Norwegian nature easier and more affordable to experience. Today, its network includes more than 600 cabins spread across mountain ranges, forests, and former farmsteads.

Article Title: China’s 16.18-km undersea high-speed rail tunnel completes 21-day cutter replacement under extreme pressure
Article Text:
Image: AI Generated

How China’s Jintang undersea tunnel completed high-pressure shield cutter replacement

Engineers replaced 104 cutting tools under high pressure

The “Deep-Sea Space Station” allows longer work shifts

China is pushing high-speed rail through underwater environments

Deep beneath the waters off eastern China, engineers are carrying out one of the most demanding stages of construction on a high-speed railway tunnel. The Jintang undersea tunnel, part of the Ningbo-Zhoushan high-speed railway in Zhejiang Province, has completed the inspection and replacement of 104 shield cutting tools after 21 days of work under intense water and soil pressure. The 16.18-kilometre tunnel is set to become the world’s longest undersea high-speed rail tunnel, linking Ningbo with Zhoushan and cutting the journey between the two cities from as much as two hours to about 26 minutes. The latest operation also tested a domestically developed saturation hyperbaric system adapted from deep-sea diving technology. The achievement comes as China continues pushing high-speed rail construction through challenging underwater environments, including the recently completed shield-machine crossing beneath the Yangtze River, another major engineering milestone highlighted by China’s State Council Information Office . The operation demonstrates how construction methods are being adapted to underwater conditions safely too.The Jintang tunnel is the critical undersea section of the Ningbo-Zhoushan high-speed railway and stretches 16.18 kilometres, including an 11.21-kilometre shield-bored section. It will connect the port city of Ningbo with the Zhoushan islands, where journeys currently rely heavily on roads and ferries. Once the railway opens, travel between Ningbo and Zhoushan is expected to take as little as 26 minutes, compared with roughly 1.5 to 2 hours today.The tunnel is being excavated from opposite shores using two super-large-diameter shield machines. One machine, Yongzhou, must bore 4,940 metres through 24 alternating layers of soft and hard rock, representing nearly 70 per cent of its route and creating severe wear on its cutting tools. Excavation progress is being monitored carefully. The geological conditions make the project particularly demanding. Rock strength along the route reaches 191 megapascals, placing some of the material in the high-strength to very-high-strength category. As the cutting head moves through alternating rock layers, its tools experience substantial mechanical stress and wear. That made the latest replacement operation necessary, but carrying out such maintenance deep beneath the seabed presented a challenge of its own. At the tunnel’s deepest point, the excavation reaches about 92 metres below sea level, where combined water and soil pressure can reach 8.5 bar. A roughly 2,000-metre section experiences pressure above 6 bar. These conditions mean that workers cannot simply enter the cutting chamber using conventional methods and carry out maintenance as they would in a normal tunnel.The latest operation involved inspecting and replacing 104 shield cutting tools over 21 days. These tools sit at the front of the tunnel-boring machine and are responsible for breaking through the rock and soil ahead of it. Their condition is critical because worn cutters can reduce excavation efficiency and make continued tunnelling more difficult. The operation was carried out under high water pressure, turning what would ordinarily be a demanding mechanical maintenance job into a complex human-safety challenge. Global Times reported that conventional compressed-air methods provide workers with only around 40 minutes of effective working time per person each day and are generally limited to depths of approximately 60 metres. The Jintang tunnel’s deeper and higher-pressure conditions required a different approach. The construction team spent three years adapting technology derived from deep-sea saturation diving. The result was described as China’s first domestically developed saturation hyperbaric system for shield tunnelling, nicknamed the “Deep-Sea Space Station” by the project team. Rather than repeatedly exposing workers to major pressure changes, the system allows them to remain in a controlled pressurised environment for extended periods.The system consists of living, transfer and control modules designed to allow workers to operate safely under the extreme conditions surrounding the tunnel boring machine. The system can accommodate nine workers for extended periods, with crew members travelling to the work face through a transfer chamber. They can work for up to eight hours at a time, allowing round-the-clock multi-shift operations for as long as 28 days. One of the key advantages is that workers undergo a single controlled decompression after completing their assignment instead of repeatedly moving between normal atmospheric pressure and the high-pressure working environment. This reduces the risks associated with frequent pressure changes and makes prolonged underwater construction work more manageable. The technology represents an unusual overlap between offshore engineering and underground construction. Techniques developed for people working at significant depths underwater have been adapted to create a controlled environment inside a tunnel-boring operation. In practical terms, the system gives engineers more time at the cutting face while reducing the number of dangerous pressure transitions workers must endure. The successful 21-day cutter replacement operation therefore represents more than routine maintenance. It provided a real-world test of whether the new system could support prolonged work under the pressure conditions encountered by the Jintang tunnel.The Jintang project forms part of a broader expansion of high-speed rail infrastructure through some of China’s most challenging terrain. The Ningbo-Zhoushan railway is designed to bring Zhoushan more directly into the national high-speed rail network, with the undersea tunnel providing a crucial connection beneath the water separating the islands from mainland Zhejiang. The project also comes shortly after another major underwater railway milestone in China. On July 31, 2026, the State Council Information Office reported that China had completed excavation of the tunnel beneath the Yangtze River for the Shanghai-Chongqing-Chengdu high-speed railway. The project uses the large-diameter shield machine Linghang and is designed for high-speed trains travelling at up to 350 kilometres per hour without slowing for the underwater section.The two projects involve different waterways and engineering challenges, but together they demonstrate the scale of China’s efforts to extend high-speed rail through difficult underwater environments. While the Yangtze project required a record-setting shield machine to pass beneath one of the country’s largest rivers, the Jintang project is tackling prolonged excavation beneath the seabed, where high rock strength and intense pressure complicate both boring and maintenance. For the Jintang tunnel, is also another step towards completing a connection expected to dramatically shorten travel between Ningbo and Zhoushan. The Yongzhou shield machine has already advanced 3,936 metres, or nearly 80 per cent of its assigned task. If construction continues as planned, the finished tunnel will not simply provide a faster route between two cities. It will also stand as a demonstration of how large-scale rail infrastructure can be built in environments where conventional tunnelling techniques reach their limits, with workers and machines operating beneath some of the most challenging pressure conditions encountered in modern rail construction.
Article Summary: Engineers replaced 104 cutting tools under high pressure. The Jintang undersea tunnel is part of the Ningbo-Zhoushan high-speed railway in Zhejiang Province. The 16.18-kilometre tunnel is set to become the world’s longest undersea high- speed rail tunnel.

Article Title: Meet Finley Holz, the Minnesota student who studied 10 years of wolf-tracking data and found deep snow can make wolves move less
Article Text:
Image AI generated

How Finley Holz used wolf-tracking and winter weather data to study wolf movement

Image AI generated

Deep snow was linked to reduced wolf movement in Minnesota

Finley Holz found wolf movement decreased as winter storms approached

Finley Holz’s wolf research earns second place in Minnesota Story Map competition

Minnesota student’s decade-long wolf research reveals effects of snow and storms

Holz combined wolf-tracking records with winter weather data, including temperature, snow depth and snowfall. Using ArcGIS Pro, he mapped wolf locations and converted them into movement data, while a Python programme helped compare movements with weather conditions. His research found that deeper snow was linked to reduced wolf movement. The study recorded a statistically significant negative correlation between snow depth and movement.However, cold snaps did not significantly affect how much the wolves moved. The research also produced an unexpected finding. Wolf movement decreased as a winter storm approached, while three days after a storm, movement was significantly below the average winter level. Holz's project was recognised in a Minnesota Story Map competition, where he placed second.Holz combined wolf-tracking information with winter weather measurements, including high and low temperatures, snow depth and snowfall events.The project used ArcGIS Pro to organise shapefiles and create maps showing wolf locations. The resulting location points were then converted into movement data. Holz also wrote a Python programme to align the wolf movements with the different winter weather conditions.The data came from wolf collar information provided by the Fond du Lac Resource Management Division. Pine Knot News, a Minnesota-based publication, reports that wildlife programme manager Michael Schrage provided wolf collar data and guidance to the students. Holz and other students also had the opportunity to collar Otter Creek wolf pups on the Fond du Lac Reservation on 5 May.One of the clearest findings from Holz's research was the relationship between snow depth and wolf movement. According to the project published in Fairfolio, titled ‘ The Effect of Winter Weather Events on Wolf (Canis lupus) Movement on the Fond du Lac Reservation’ , Holz's second hypothesis was supported: wolves moved less as snow depth increased. The study found a statistically significant negative correlation between snow depth and wolf movement. In simple terms, the data showed that as the snow became deeper, the distance wolves travelled per movement decreased.The finding in similar terms, stating that Holz "found that winter cold snaps have no effect on wolf movement" but that there was "a negative correlation between snow depth and wolf movement: the deeper the snow, the less the wolves moved." Holz had also expected extreme cold to affect wolf movement. His third hypothesis predicted that wolves would move the least during a cold snap. However, the results did not support this idea. The Fairfolio project says there was no difference in wolf movement during a cold snap compared with normal winter movement. That meant that extremely cold periods, at least within the conditions examined in the study, did not produce the reduction in movement Holz had expected.Another unexpected finding came from the relationship between wolf movement and winter storms. Holz originally hypothesised that wolves would travel the furthest immediately after a storm. Instead, the data showed that their movement declined around the time of a storm.According to the project abstract, "Three days after the storm had passed, the wolves moved significantly less than the average winter movement (p<.001)." After that period, their movement returned to the normal winter pattern. The study also found something Holz described as surprising: wolf movement decreased each day as a winter storm approached.The project says this "appears to indicate that the wolves were able to sense the oncoming storm before it arrived."Holz's wolf research also became part of a successful Minnesota Story Map competition. Two Cloquet High School students and a Hermantown student with Cloquet connections won the top three places in the competition. Hermantown freshman Gabriel Bradley came first, while Cloquet sophomores Finley Holz and Melanie Buhs placed second and third.The Minnesota Alliance for Geographic Education competition challenges students to conduct research and present their findings through an ArcGIS Online story map.Holz's project focused on the effect of winter weather events on wolf movement, while Bradley's project examined factors affecting wolf pack den relocation.Holz's project provides a detailed look at how winter conditions can influence wolf movement in northeastern Minnesota. Rather than finding that every form of severe winter weather caused wolves to travel less, the research showed a more specific pattern. Increasing snow depth was associated with reduced wolf movement, while cold snaps alone did not significantly change movement.The study also raised a new question about how wolves respond to approaching storms. The observation that movement decreased before a storm arrived suggests that further research could investigate whether wolves respond to changes in atmospheric or environmental conditions before severe weather reaches the area.For a high-school research project, Holz's work combined a decade of wildlife-tracking information with geographic mapping, weather data and computer analysis to examine the behaviour of an important northern predator.
Article Summary: Finley Holz combined wolf-tracking and winter weather data to study wolf movement in Minnesota. He found that deeper snow was linked to reduced wolf movement. Wolf movement decreased as a winter storm approached, while three days after a storm, movement was significantly below the average winter level.
