Article Title: Scientists planted 133 portable seismometers around Yellowstone’s Old Faithful for two weeks; tiny ground vibrations revealed an underground hot-water reservoir holding about 79 million gallons
Article Text:
Old Faithful Geyser EruptionPhoto: Canva

Why Old Faithful’s underground system was a mystery

Turning noise into a map: the 133-seismometer experiment

What the tremors revealed: a giant hidden reservoir

Why this matters for science and park management

Old Faithful may be the world’s most famous geyser, but until recently, no one had a clear picture of the “plumbing” that powers its eruptions. In a landmark 2017 study titled 'Anatomy of Old Faithful From Subsurface Seismic Imaging of the Yellowstone Upper Geyser Basin', University of Utah scientists deployed 133 small, portable seismometers around Old Faithful and nearby Geyser Hill for two weeks, listening to the faint hum of the ground between eruptions. By turning everyday micro-vibrations, caused by wind, water, tourists, and the geyser’s own boiling, into a usable signal, the team mapped a hidden reservouir of hot water beneath the surface. Their analysis suggests the reservoir can hold roughly 300,000 cubic meters of water, or about 79 million gallons. Based on the reportings from the University of Utah and the U.S. Geological Survey’s Yellowstone Volcano Observatory, here's more details about the discovery:Old Faithful erupts like clockwork every 44 to 125 minutes, drawing millions of visitors to Yellowstone National Park each year. Yet despite its fame, the near-surface geology and fluid pathways feeding the geyser were poorly understood. Deep magma reservoirs 5–40 km below the park provide heat, but the shallow “plumbing” that channels hot water to the vent had never been mapped in detail. Traditional seismic methods that rely on large earthquakes or active sources (like hammer strikes or small explosions) aren’t ideal in a sensitive, crowded tourist area.The National Park Service specifically asked researchers to survey the Old Faithful area to better manage buildings and walkways constructed over thermal features that can create excessive subsurface heat.To capture the subtle signals, the University of Utah team used compact, autonomous seismometers developed for the oil and gas industry. Each unit is a white canister about six inches high, self-contained and inexpensive compared to traditional instruments that can cost over $10,000. In 2015, researchers placed 133 of these sensors around Old Faithful and Geyser Hill for a two-week campaign, creating a dense network capable of detecting tiny ground movements.Instead of creating their own seismic source, the scientists treated ambient noise as data. They used continuous ground shaking from humans, cars, wind, water, and Yellowstone’s hydrothermal activity, then extracted coherent signals from the background vibration. Doctoral student Sin-Mei Wu and co-author Fan-Chi Lin developed analysis methods that correlated signals from sensors near persistent hydrothermal sources to others across the array, effectively using the geyser system itself as a seismic source. This approach allowed them to image shallow structures without disturbing the fragile environment of the Upper Geyser Basin.The sensors recorded a striking pattern: bursts of intense seismic tremors around Old Faithful lasting about 60 minutes, separated by roughly 30 minutes of quiet. Counterintuitively, the eruption does not occur at the peak of shaking but at the end, just before the tremors subside. After an eruption, the geyser’s underground cavity refills with hot water. As it fills, pressurized bubbles rise, cool rapidly, and implode; the energy from these implosions generates the pre-eruption tremors.When analyzing the data, the team noticed that tremor signals from Old Faithful were not reaching the western boardwalk. Seismic waves from another hydrothermal feature to the north also slowed and scattered in nearly the same area. With the dense sensor network, they could pinpoint the shape, size, and location of the anomaly: Old Faithful’s hydrothermal reservoir. Wu estimates the reservoir—a network of cracks and fractures through which water flows, is about 200 meters in diameter, slightly larger than the University of Utah’s Rice-Eccles Stadium, and can hold approximately 300,000 cubic meters of water, or more than 79 million gallons. By comparison, each eruption releases only around 30 cubic meters (nearly 8,000 gallons), meaning the reservoir is vastly larger than any single eruption.Mapping Old Faithful’s underground system does more than satisfy curiosity. It helps park managers understand where heat and fluid flow beneath buildings, walkways, and visitor areas, informing safer infrastructure planning in one of the world’s most visited geothermal zones. The study also demonstrates a powerful, low-impact method for imaging shallow geology in sensitive environments by leveraging ambient noise instead of active sources.For researchers, the work opens new questions about how subsurface structures change over time and how seismic waves propagate through hydrothermal systems. The team returned for additional surveys in 2016 and planned further deployments, aiming to produce even higher-resolution images and explore other basins like Norris, the park’s hottest geothermal area. As Fan-Chi Lin noted, breakthroughs in Yellowstone depend on both new techniques and long-term relationships with the park: a reminder that some of the most iconic natural wonders still have secrets waiting beneath the surface.
Article Summary: University of Utah scientists deployed 133 small, portable seismometers around Old Faithful and nearby Geyser Hill for two weeks. By turning everyday micro- vibrations, caused by wind, water, tourists, and the geyser’s own boiling, the team mapped a hidden reservouir of hot water beneath the surface.

Article Title: In 2012, a retired Florida art professor began cementing discarded bottles into his yard: more than 6,000 bottles, later, he built a house, lighthouse, and giant geodesic sphere
Article Text:
Representation of an artist building a lighthouse from discarded glass bottles. Image Credits: ChatGPT.

A retirement project takes shape

From bottle house to

bottle lighthouse

Glass bottles collected around a public recycling bin, highlighting the scale of discarded glass and the importance of proper collection and recycling. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons.

A backyard becomes an artwork

In 2012, retired art professor Leon Wiesener set out to build a house from glass bottles in his small Florida town. Just 11 months later, he had transformed more than 6,000 discarded bottles into a pentagonal structure in his backyard. The project soon grew. Wiesener added a 15-foot lighthouse with a working revolving light, along with giant geometric sculptures and other outdoor artworks. What began as a retirement project eventually became one of Carrabelle’s most unusual landmarks.According to Atlas Obscura’s account of the Carrabelle Bottle House, Leon Wiesener built the pentagon-shaped structure using more than 6,000 glass bottles. Its walls are 12 feet long and 8 feet high, while the roof rises 14 feet above the ground. Antique bottles line the tops of the walls, and wide-mouth jars are set horizontally to provide storage. Wiesener also incorporated handmade German stained glass and colourful round lenses from school buses and fire trucks, adding light and vibrant colour to the structure.Wiesener has said that the idea came to him suddenly in 2012.His interest in bottle buildings was not entirely accidental. As an artist and former set painter, he was familiar with unusual materials and visual effects, but the bottle house also became a practical experiment in what could be built by hand. He collected bottles from a variety of sources. Friends and neighbours donated them, while others came from recycling centres and what Wiesener described as dumpster diving. He even placed an advertisement in a local newspaper seeking bottles. The collection eventually grew to include thousands of beer and wine bottles in a range of shapes, sizes, and colours.The bottles served a practical purpose as well as an aesthetic one: their coloured glass filtered daylight into the structure, while wide-mouth jars were set into the walls to provide storage. This approach reflects a broader interest in giving waste materials new uses in construction. Research published in Construction and Building Materials has explored ways of converting waste glass into construction materials, noting its potential to reduce demand for conventional resources while addressing the problem of glass waste. Wiesener’s approach differs from these engineered systems because he used intact bottles rather than processing glass into aggregates or powders, but the underlying principle is similar: a material normally regarded as waste can be transformed into a useful and functional element through thoughtful design.The bottle house was only the beginning of Wiesener’s experiments with glass. He later expanded the backyard collection with a 15-foot-tall bottle lighthouse, a playful nod to Carrabelle’s maritime identity and its historic Crooked River Lighthouse. Unlike a purely decorative structure, Wiesener’s lighthouse features a working revolving light at the top, making it both a functional feature and a striking piece of folk art. The garden also contains several large geometric sculptures, including a giant static geodesic sphere made from layers of smaller spheres, which Wiesener described as an abstract self-portrait representing his life. Another, roughly eight-foot-wide kinetic sphere incorporates coloured glass panels and mirrors and rotates on a stand, scattering reflected light across the garden. Together, these creations show how Wiesener continued to experiment with bottles and other discarded materials long after completing the house, turning them into imaginative structures that connect his artistic interests with Carrabelle’s coastal characterThe bottle house has attracted visitors from beyond Carrabelle, with its unusual appearance and construction history making it a local roadside curiosity. Wiesener continued adding to the property, gradually transforming the area around the house into an outdoor gallery filled with glass, metal, household objects, and other salvaged materials. The house also reflects a broader tradition of incorporating discarded bottles into buildings for decoration, natural light, and, in some cases, construction. Rather than being presented as a large-scale solution to glass waste, Wiesener’s project is better understood as a personal artistic experiment that gave discarded bottles new uses. More than 6,000 bottles became part of the house, while other salvaged objects were incorporated into artworks and structures throughout the property. Together, the house, lighthouse, and geometric sculptures illustrate how Wiesener turned everyday materials into distinctive features of a landscape shaped by his artistic vision.
Article Summary: Leon Wiesener built the pentagon-shaped structure using more than 6,000 glass bottles. The bottles served a practical purpose as well as an aesthetic one. Antique bottles line the tops of the walls, and wide-mouth jars are set horizontally to provide storage. The garden also contains several large geometric sculptures, including a giant static geodesic sphere.

Article Title: In the 1950s, Lilley Cornett refused timber developers for his Kentucky forest; his legacy survives today at Lilley Cornett Woods among 400-year-old trees
Article Text:
AI Representation: An ancient Kentucky forest stands preserved beneath towering trees. Image credits: Chatgpt

Lilley

Cornett

Woods Appalachian Research Station Initiated into the

Old-Growth Forest

Network

Cornett protected the woodland from commercial timber harvesting

Topography shaped the forest's nine plant communities

The Lilley Cornett Woods: A Stable Mixed Mesophytic Forest in Kentucky

Old-growth conditions support woodland salamander research

“Environmental Gradients in Old-Growth Appalachian Forest Predict Fine-Scale Distribution, Co-occurrence and Density of

Woodland Salamanders

,”

A white oak dating to 1669 is the oldest documented tree

The protected forest helps preserve an older eastern Kentucky landscape

Lilley Cornett Woods, located in Letcher County in eastern Kentucky, preserves approximately 252 acres of old-growth mixed mesophytic forest. According to Eastern Kentucky University’s article,, the forest contains trees dating to as early as 1669, including a white oak that is more than 350 years old. It is also designated a National Natural Landmark.According to Eastern Kentucky University’s historical account, the woodland takes its name from Lilley Cornett, who purchased the property shortly after World War I and chose to protect its trees from timber cutters rather than allow them to be harvested. After he died, his family continued to preserve the woodland until it was sold to the Commonwealth of Kentucky in 1969. Afterwards, management was transferred to Eastern Kentucky University and it now runs this place as the Lilley Cornett Woods Appalachian Ecological Research Station.Cornett's decision to preserve the woodland was significant because much of eastern Kentucky had already been heavily timbered. The central portion of Lilley Cornett Woods, which makes up the old-growth area, has never been harvested, although parts of the forest have seen some human intervention.Livestock grazed in the understory until the 1950s. Some dead or dying American chestnuts were removed after chestnut blight affected the species. None of these interventions had caused commercial harvesting of the old-growth. After Cornett died, his family continued caring for the land until they found a way to preserve it. After the property was sold to the Commonwealth of Kentucky in 1969, Eastern Kentucky University took over management. The property now covers about 659 acres, including 252 acres of old-growth forest. The entire property is not old-growth forest.William H. Martin examined the ecological character of Lilley Cornett Woods in his 1975 study . He identified nine forest communities and examined how their distribution related to the woodland’s topography. In Martin’s study, trees measuring more than 12.5 centimetres in diameter at breast height had an average density of 290 stems per hectare. Beech-dominated communities were widespread and represented approximately half of the upland stable segment of the Woods. Oak communities were second in area and occupied the more xeric sites. Topography helped shape these differences because changes in slope and landscape position created different environments. Eastern hemlock communities were found in the woodland, while more wind-protected areas contained sugar maple, basswood and tulip poplar. Martin’s study suggests that the significance of Lilley Cornett Woods cannot be judged by tree age alone.The forest has also served as a subject for studying the influence of old-growth forest conditions on wildlife. In an Ecology and Evolution study titledscientists analyzed woodland salamanders at Lilley Cornett Woods. This research involved 102 hectares of old-growth forest land. The authors note that the area had no timber-harvest history, although livestock grazed there until the 1950s. The scientists studied how environmental factors affected salamander distribution, co-occurrence and density.The scientists used permanent sampling plots to assess vegetation, leaf litter, rocky cover and topography. The study found that variation in environmental conditions corresponded to variation in salamander distribution and density. These results offer another perspective on the woodland's ecological significance. Its importance lies not only in preserving old trees but also in maintaining the variety of environmental conditions created by the mature forest ecosystem.Eastern Kentucky University says a white oak dating to 1669 is the oldest recorded tree at Lilley Cornett Woods. By 2026, the tree would be more than 350 years old, approximately 357 years, assuming 1669 as the starting date. The tree's age shows that it existed long before the current landscape around the preserve took shape. This tree also gives scientists a very old example of the forests that once covered much of eastern Kentucky.An EKU flora study documented 516 vascular plant species at Lilley Cornett Woods, representing 92 families and 297 genera. This highlights the preserve's biological diversity. The old trees and diverse plant life have made the preserve a valuable site for scientific study. Martin studied the structure and distribution of the forest communities, while the salamander study examined how old-growth conditions affected wildlife.The Lilley Cornett Woods Preserve now stands not only as a place of conservation but as a site of study as well. The old-growth component contains trees that have been growing there for hundreds of years, while the overall tract serves as habitat and a research area. Therefore, the memory of Cornett is connected with more than simply trees. Cornett's decision to protect the forest preserved a community that remained available for study after commercial logging elsewhere had ended. Today, Lilley Cornett Woods Preserve allows scientists to study one of the last remaining examples of old-growth Appalachia in eastern Kentucky.
Article Summary: Lilley Cornett Woods, located in Letcher County in eastern Kentucky, preserves approximately 252 acres of old-growth mixed mesophytic forest. The forest contains trees dating to as early as 1669, including a white oak that is more than 350 years old. The protected forest helps preserve an older eastern Kentucky landscape.

Article Title: In 2006, Steve and Dianne White bought 86 acres in Fulton County, Illinois; 16 years later, it held wetlands, prairie and sightings of 71 bird species
Article Text:
AI Representation: A restored wetland at 'Bout Broke Farm. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

The 86-acre farm combines production land with conservation areas

Wetlands became part of the farm's water and habitat management

Tree planting expanded the property's wooded habitat

Steve White recorded approximately 71 bird species

AI Representation: A restored wetland at 'Bout Broke Farm. Image credits: Wikimedia Commons

Conservation programmes supported work on the private farm

When Steve and Dianne White purchased an 86-acre property in Fulton County, Illinois, in 2006, it had been used for agriculture for decades and showed signs of erosion. By 2022, the property, known as Bout Broke Farm, included cropland, forest, wetlands, pollinator habitat and prairie. Steve had recorded approximately 71 bird species there. The transformation is documented in a USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service feature on the property, titled '‘Bout Broke Farm.They kept some of their land for farming while converting the rest for conservation use. This created a diverse landscape, with cropland combined with natural areas that provided a variety of wildlife habitats. The Whites' conservation work spans soil and water conservation as well as habitat improvement. At the same time, the approach allowed the Whites to support wildlife while continuing agricultural production on the property.Wetlands are another important part of conservation at Bout Broke Farm, helping manage water and soil on the property. A pond and surrounding vegetation also provide habitat for wildlife on the farm. That adds aquatic and wetland habitat to the woodland and prairie already on the farm. The Illinois Department of Natural Resources’ 2022 CREP newsletter provides background on the Conservation Reserve Enhancement Program, including its role in protecting water quality, reducing runoff and establishing wildlife habitat on private agricultural land.The publication described conservation work involving the Whites and showed how private farmland can support broader habitat and water-quality goals. In addition, the wetlands and pond offer chances to see wildlife that favors water habitat over open cropland. Their addition provides another habitat type to land that was once used only for agriculture.Tree planting was another part of the Whites' conservation work. The developing woodland added areas of tree cover to the farm and complemented the existing open habitats. Trees can provide food, nesting locations and shelter for wildlife, while also contributing to soil protection. On this property, the wooded areas form part of a broader landscape that includes prairie, wetlands and cropland. The Whites' work with trees also received recognition when they were named 2022 Outstanding Tree Farmers by the Illinois Tree Farm Program, according to the NRCS feature on the property. The recognition reflected their efforts to incorporate tree stewardship into the management of the property. Pollinator habitat was another component of the conservation work. The farm contains areas managed for pollinators, adding flowering vegetation and additional habitat alongside the agricultural fields. Rather than relying on a single conservation measure, the Whites combined several approaches across the 86 acres.Wildlife changes can be seen from the perspective of Steve White's bird observations. In 2022, he was able to identify about 71 different species of birds. Among the birds, Steve White observed species typical for various ecosystems, such as wetlands, open spaces and forestland. These species included such birds as bald eagles, bobwhite quail, blue-winged teal, wood ducks, great blue herons, barred owls, eastern bluebirds, indigo buntings and pileated woodpeckers. Steve White's count is based on his own observations, not a formal biodiversity survey.The variety of bird species suggests the property supports a range of habitats. At the same time, there are prairies and other open spaces that attract certain species of birds. Forests also attract woodland species of birds. The variety of birds points to conservation benefits on the farm, though Steve's count is informal rather than a scientific survey.The Whites' conservation work received support from federal and state programs. The Natural Resources Conservation Service offered technical help to the farmers in their conservation efforts. The property was also involved in programs aimed at improving habitat and managing natural resources on private farmland. Such programs can help landowners address soil erosion, water quality and wildlife habitat without giving up farming. The program is part of a broader effort to protect environmentally sensitive private land by helping landowners adopt these practices voluntarily. These programs were the means of incorporating the conservation practices into the general management of the farm by the Whites.By 2022, Bout Broke Farm had become a conservation landscape rather than an agricultural-only one. Agriculture continued to be practiced on the farm as wetlands, prairie, woodland and pollinator habitat were introduced to achieve other conservation objectives. The change was not achieved by stopping agriculture on the property but through combining the two on different portions of the farm. Steve's record of about 71 bird species shows the range of wildlife using the farm. The wetlands, tree planting areas, prairie and pollinator habitats exemplify some of the various conservation efforts undertaken on the land. By changing how different parts of the 86 acres are used, the Whites created a landscape that supports agriculture while also providing wildlife habitat.
Article Summary: Steve and Dianne White purchased an 86-acre property in Fulton County, Illinois, in 2006. By 2022, the property, known as Bout Broke Farm, included cropland, forest, wetlands, pollinator habitat and prairie. Steve had recorded approximately 71 bird species there.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Article Title: Food safety starts before cooking: Simple habits that matter
Article Text:
Food safety habits start before cooking

At the supermarket

The journey home matters too

Good food habits begin in the kitchen

Food safety doesn't end when dinner is over

Small choices often make the biggest difference

Every safe meal is built on everyday habits

Disclaimer: The above is non-editorial content, and TIL does not guarantee, vouch or endorse any of it. Please take all steps necessary to ascertain that any information and content provided is correct, updated, and verified.

When families sit down to eat together, most conversations revolve around how the food tastes. Was the curry just right? Is the chapati soft enough? Has everyone taken a second helping?Yet, long before anyone takes the first bite, dozens of small decisions have already shaped that meal. Choosing the right products, storing them correctly, maintaining kitchen hygiene and handling leftovers safely may not receive the same attention as the recipe itself, but these everyday habits play an important role in protecting the food families share.Food safety, after all, doesn't begin in the kitchen. It begins much earlier.Every grocery trip involves countless choices. While price, freshness and nutritional value often influence buying decisions, it's equally important to look closely at the condition of packaged foods.Consumers should check that packaging is intact, seals have not been tampered with, and expiry or best-before dates are clearly within range. Storage instructions on the label also offer useful guidance, especially for products that require refrigeration after purchase.These simple checks help ensure food reaches home in the condition intended by the manufacturer.Food can spend considerable time between the checkout counter and the refrigerator. During warmer months or longer commutes, keeping perishable products out of the temperature danger zone becomes especially important.Planning grocery shopping so refrigerated and frozen foods are picked up last, avoiding unnecessary delays and refrigerating them promptly on reaching home can help preserve food quality and safety.Preparing meals involves much more than following a recipe. Everyday kitchen hygiene can significantly reduce the risk of contamination.Many of these everyday habits align with the World Health Organization 's Five Keys to Safer Food , a globally recognised framework that encourages keeping food clean, preventing cross-contamination, cooking thoroughly, storing food at safe temperatures and using safe water and fresh ingredients.Rather than viewing these as strict rules, they can become simple habits that fit naturally into everyday cooking.Once the meal is served, food safety continues.Leftovers should be refrigerated promptly in clean containers, opened products should be stored according to the instructions provided, and food should be reheated thoroughly before consumption. These small practices not only help maintain quality but can also reduce food waste by ensuring food remains safe to eat.This idea that the smallest actions often carry the greatest significance is echoed in a recent consumer awareness campaign featuring culinary creator Nisha Madhulika. The video reminds viewers that while recipes may earn compliments, it is the thoughtful choices made before, during and after cooking that quietly help protect the people we care about.Supported by ExxonMobil Signature Polymers as part of its consumer education initiative, the campaign also highlights the role of food packaging in the broader food safety journey. Advancements in polymer solutions have enabled packaging that helps preserve freshness and maintain product integrity as food moves through the supply chain. Once it reaches the home, however, safe handling practices remain equally important.Food safety is rarely the result of one big decision. Instead, it is shaped by a series of small, mindful choices, from checking a package before placing it in the shopping cart to washing hands before cooking, separating raw and cooked foods and storing leftovers correctly.Individually, these actions may seem routine. Together, they become one of the simplest ways families can care for one another. Because when it comes to protecting loved ones, food hygiene truly begins long before the first bite.
Article Summary: Food safety is rarely the result of one big decision. Instead, it is shaped by a series of small, mindful choices. Choosing the right products, storing them correctly, maintaining kitchen hygiene and handling leftovers safely may not receive the same attention as the recipe itself.

Article Title: Swiggy Dineout launches ‘Order-in-Cinemas’ feature to let moviegoers order food from their seats: Here’s how it will work
Article Text:
How Swiggy Dineout’s Order-in-Cinemas works

Swiggy Dineout partners with cinema PoS providers

“We have recently partnered with Swiggy Dineout for integrating this service into our impact ticketing solution at the cinemas.

It's a very simple and elegant solution and I'm sure this is going to give value to the cinema as well as the viewer and improve their overall movie watching experience. We have already started the integration process, and it will be a very seamless experience for the audience, providing a wider assortment and availability of food on the seat itself.

”

“We have integrated the Swiggy Dineout feature and it's getting a great response. Everyone is loving it- customers are very excited as they can order on Swiggy, and the food will be delivered to their seats directly. Thank you so much Swiggy for this support,”

Swiggy Dineout has launched an ‘Order-in-Cinemas’ feature that lets moviegoers order food from their seats instead of standing in queues at cinema halls. The QR-based feature is being introduced in partnership with Cinepolis and Asian Cinemas, allowing users to scan a code, browse the cinema’s menu, place an order and pay through the Swiggy Dineout app.The feature is currently being rolled out across multiple screens, with Swiggy Dineout also working with PoS aggregator Impact, owned and operated by UFO Moviez, and cinema software provider Showbizz. The company said integration with multiple PoS aggregators is underway.The ordering process follows four steps: Scan, Browse, Order & Pay, and Delivery. Moviegoers can scan a QR code placed inside the cinema hall, open the cinema’s menu through Swiggy Dineout, select their food and pay from their seats. The order is then delivered directly to the customer's seat.For Cinepolis and Asian Cinemas, the Swiggy Dineout app will also show information about upcoming movie releases, trailers, posters, booking links, special screenings, events and promotional offers.The feature also allows cinemas to recommend food and beverage combos and offer additional items to moviegoers through upselling and cross-selling options.Swiggy Dineout has partnered with Impact and Showbizz to connect the ordering system with cinema PoS infrastructure. Impact is owned and operated by UFO Moviez, while Showbizz provides cinema software solutions for PoS aggregation.Rajesh Mishra, Founder and MD of UFO Moviez, said the integration with Swiggy Dineout had already started for the company's Impact ticketing solution.He said:Asian Cinemas has also integrated the feature, according to Jyesth Narang, Executive Director of Asian Cinemas.he notedSwiggy Dineout said the service is also intended to give cinemas another way to generate food and beverage orders while allowing PoS players to integrate the feature into their existing systems.

The QR-based feature is being introduced in partnership with Cinepolis and Asian Cinemas, allowing users to scan a code, browse the cinema’s menu, place an order and pay. The ordering process follows four steps: Scan, Browse, Order & Pay, and Delivery.

Article Title: Xiaomi launches Mijia Smart Air Purifier 6 and Air Purifier 4 Compact in India, price starts at Rs 7,999
Article Text:
Mijia Smart Air Purifier 6 features

Mijia Smart Air Purifier 4 Compact features

Mijia Smart Air Purifier 6 and 4 Compact price in India

Expanding its product range, Xiaomi has launched its first device under smart home and lifestyle sub-brand, Mijia. The company has introduced the Mijia Smart Air Purifier 6 and Mijia Smart Air Purifier 4 Compact in India. The two air purifiers are designed for different room sizes and come with air-quality monitoring, app controls and multiple purification modes. The Mijia Smart Air Purifier 6 is aimed at larger spaces, while the Air Purifier 4 Compact is designed for bedrooms. Alongside, Xiaomi has also announced the return of the Xiaomi Smart Air Purifier 4 Lite to its India lineup.The Mijia Smart Air Purifier 6 is designed for spaces of up to 940 sq. ft., based on two air changes per hour. It has a Particle CADR of 443 m³/h and a Formaldehyde CADR of 218 m³/h.The purifier uses a five-stage PentaClean purification system that combines filtration, activated carbon, UV-C light and Negative Ion technology. Xiaomi says it can help reduce dust, pollen, pet dander, smoke, formaldehyde and other airborne pollutants.It also comes with a colour display that shows PM2.5 and PM1 levels, temperature, humidity and air-quality information.Users can control the purifier through the Xiaomi Home app and use compatible Amazon Alexa and Google Assistant voice controls.For night-time use, the purifier has a Sleep Mode with noise levels of around 32dB(A).The Mijia Smart Air Purifier 4 Compact is designed for rooms that are more than 400 sq. ft in size. It uses a 3-in-1 filtration system that Xiaomi says can capture 99.97% of particles as small as 0.3 microns.It is aimed at smaller spaces such as bedrooms, kids' rooms, study areas and home offices. The purifier also has TÜV Rheinland Allergy Care Certification and is designed to filter common airborne allergens, including pollen and dust.The device comes with a four-colour air-quality indicator and an Auto Mode that adjusts the purification speed based on detected air quality. It also offers Sleep and Manual modes.Weighing 2.2kg, the purifier can be placed on a desk, table or floor. Its Sleep Mode operates at 20dB and turns off the display. Like the larger model, it can also be controlled through the Xiaomi Home app and supports compatible Alexa and Google Assistant controls.The Mijia Smart Air Purifier 6 is priced at Rs 19,999, while the Mijia Smart Air Purifier 4 Compact costs Rs 7,999. Xiaomi is also bringing back the Xiaomi Smart Air Purifier 4 Lite at Rs 12,999.All three air purifiers will go on sale in India starting September 2, 2026, through mi.com, Amazon, Flipkart, Blinkit, Xiaomi Retail and Xiaomi Exclusive stores.

The two air purifiers are designed for different room sizes and come with air- quality monitoring, app controls and multiple purification modes. Alongside, Xiaomi has also announced the return of the Xiaomi Smart Air purifier 4 Lite to its India lineup.

Article Title: China’s AliExpress caught using audio trick to track visitors; discovered after it broke researcher’s headphones
Article Text:
Representative Image

“audio trick”

How AliExpress used browser audio fingerprinting

“The oscillator generates a known waveform,”

“The analyser measures the result after it has passed through the browser’s audio implementation, and the script reads frequency data from it.”

Firefox and Chrome have protections against audio fingerprinting

AliExpress uses multiple browser tracking methods

Chinese retailer AliExpress has been found using anthat can fingerprint visitors by analysing sounds processed by their web browsers. The technique measures inaudible audio signals and was discovered by researcher Matthew Callaghan after visiting the AliExpress website repeatedly caused his phone audio to stop playing through his Bluetooth headphones.According to a report by Ars Technica, Callaghan said the problem occurred because his headphones support multipoint connections, allowing them to connect to his phone and PC at the same time. He had configured them to play audio from his phone unless his PC was producing sound. Each time he opened AliExpress, the phone audio stopped, and it resumed after he closed the tab containing the website.While investigating the issue, Callaghan found two highly obfuscated scripts on the AliExpress homepage. Together, the scripts generated a graph that analysed WebAudio readings from the browser.The system used an oscillator to generate Sawtooth waves, a type of waveform commonly produced by digital audio systems. An analyser then measured the resulting frequency data after the signal passed through the browser's audio implementation.Callaghan wrote.The scripts set the audio gain to zero, meaning the visitor could not hear the signal. The audio graph remained connected to the selected system audio, however, allowing the browser to process the signal before sending the resulting information to AliExpress.The technique can be used for audio fingerprinting because differences in the way browsers and systems process audio can produce identifiable results. Those differences were once large enough to create many distinct signatures when combined with variations in CPUs and other system characteristics.Firefox addressed the technique beginning with version 118, released in 2023. The browser began using its own consistent math libraries rather than relying on operating-system-supplied libraries.Tom Ritter, a Firefox developer who has also volunteered for the Tor Project, said the change reduced the amount of identifying information available from the technique enough to prevent it from working.The technique is also ineffective in Chrome because Google's browser uses its own libraries, according to a Google spokesperson. Safari users are likely protected for the same reason, although Apple did not immediately confirm this.The audio technique is only one of several metrics Callaghan identified in AliExpress' tracking scripts. The other methods he found included:* Canvas rendering and `toDataURL()`* WebGL renderer information, extensions and shader precision* Audio oscillator and analyzer output* Screen and viewport dimensions* Device pixel ratio* Hardware concurrency and device memory* Installed browser plugins* Supported audio and video formats* WebRTC behavior* Browser performance timing* Mouse, touch, focus and scroll events* Device motion and orientation* Properties commonly associated with browser automationTogether, these measurements can provide information about a visitor's browser and device. Callaghan said the WebAudio method appears to be an older fingerprinting technique that may have remained in AliExpress' code despite browser changes that have reduced its effectiveness.
Article Summary: Chinese retailer AliExpress has been found using anthat can fingerprint visitors by analysing sounds processed by their web browsers. The technique measures inaudible audio signals and was discovered by researcher Matthew Callaghan after visiting the AliExpress website repeatedly caused his phone audio to stop playing.
